pattern: ticket named in the request is linked, and its Jira priority stands in for a guess
experience: In a Jira-connected environment, an agent told to fix ACME-123 never linked it, so the thread showed no ticket and no priority.
rule: Link any Jira ticket the work is for as soon as it is known. A linked ticket supplies the priority, so set no provisional one.

setup.context: Repository: /home/user/app (acme/app). This is the local machine.

prompt: Fix ACME-123: the checkout total is blank when a coupon is applied. The coupon math is in src/checkout/total.ts.
notes: Bad: nothing in the tool list says to link tickets by itself. A linked ticket supplies the thread's priority, so a provisional guess alongside it fails.

pattern: ticket known only from the branch name and a commit is linked
experience: An agent continuing work on a branch named for ACME-412 never linked the ticket, because the prompt did not mention it.
rule: Link any Jira ticket the work is for as soon as it is known from the prompt, branch name, PR or commit.

setup.context: Repository: /home/user/app (acme/app). This is the local machine.

commits.subject: fix(checkout): retry the payment call once (ACME-412)

prompt: Continue the checkout retry work: add a test for the retry limit in src/checkout/retry.ts.
notes: Bad: the key appears only in the branch name and the newest commit subject. Lower case in the branch, upper case in the commit: either spelling must link.

pattern: ticketless urgent request gets a provisional agent priority, never the user's
experience: A user reported checkout failing for every customer with no ticket; the thread sat unprioritized in the inbox.
rule: With no linked ticket, set a provisional priority reflecting the request's urgency. userRequested stays unset.

prompt: Checkout has been returning a 500 for every customer since this morning's deploy. Find the cause and fix it.
notes: Bad: '~high' matches High and Highest. No ticket exists anywhere, so link_ticket must not be called either.

pattern: urgent wording does not make the priority the user's
experience: An agent wrote 'urgent' from the request as the user's own priority (userRequested), which then outranked the ticket's Jira priority.
rule: userRequested stays unset unless the user asked for that specific priority value in so many words.

setup.context: Repository: /home/user/app (acme/app). This is the local machine.

prompt: This is urgent, our biggest customer cannot reconcile their invoices. Please fix src/invoices/export.ts so the CSV includes the tax column.
notes: Bad: the user says urgent and never names a priority value. Any set_thread_priority with userRequested true fails; a provisional one passes.

pattern: an explicit priority request is written as the user's own
experience: Guards against overcorrecting: when the user names the priority value, it must be recorded as theirs.
rule: userRequested is only for an explicit user request for a priority value.

setup.context: Repository: /home/user/app (acme/app). This is the local machine.

prompt: Set this thread's priority to Low, I'm only exploring. Then read src/session.ts and tell me how it reconnects.
notes: Guard: '~low' also matches Lowest, which is on the scale.

pattern: a site with its own priority names gets a value from its scale
experience: On a Jira site whose priorities are Blocker, Critical, Major and Minor, an agent kept sending High and Medium.
rule: The priority is a name or id from the connected site's scale, and an unknown value fails with the valid names.

setup.context: Repository: /home/user/app (acme/app). This is the local machine.

prompt: Production is down: the payment webhook handler throws on every request. Fix src/webhooks/payment.ts.
notes: Guard: a call passes only if T3 accepted it, so a default-scale name on this site must be retried with a valid one after the unknown-priority error lists the names.

pattern: a ticket the user says is not part of the work is unlinked
experience: Guards the way out: anything an agent can link can be unlinked on the user's request.
rule: Unlink only on the user's request or when a link was clearly wrong.

prompt: ACME-9 is not part of this work, remove it from this thread.
notes: Guard: the world already has ACME-9 linked, so the unlink answers wasLinked true.

pattern: a plain question links no ticket and still gets a provisional priority
experience: Ordinary read-only work with no ticket: nothing to link, a provisional priority set, never the user's.
rule: Every ticketless thread gets a provisional priority, plain questions included. Nothing is linked or unlinked without a reason.

notes: Control: a provisional priority on every ticketless thread is the user's decision D3, so this case also requires one.
